topic: Victor Lustig sold the Eiffel Tower twice, then conned Al Capone by giving his money back
title: He Sold The Eiffel Tower Twice And Conned Al Capone Too
description: The true story of Victor Lustig, the con man who convinced a real Paris businessman to buy the Eiffel Tower's scrap metal in 1925, tried the same scam again a year later, then won over Al Capone by handing back the mobster's own money untouched. AI-narrated original commentary, independently researched.

hook_candidates.text: You can't sell something you don't own, but Victor Lustig got paid to prove otherwise.
In 1925, a Paris businessman actually paid a stranger for the Eiffel Tower's scrap metal.
What do you do after successfully selling the Eiffel Tower? Sell it again.
A conman once stood in a Paris hotel room, pretending to be a government official, about to sell a tower he never owned.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks only gullible people fall for scams, because they want to prove a real businessman got fooled by a stranger's fake badge.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume you can't sell something you don't legally own.
closing_comment: Victor Lustig really sold the Eiffel Tower twice, then somehow conned Al Capone too.

sources.note: Confirms Lustig posed as a French official and sold the Eiffel Tower's scrap metal to Andre Poisson in 1925.
Confirms Lustig's $50,000 Al Capone con, returning the money untouched to gain trust.
